beats.title: Call to order — the agenda
beats.shows: the CEO opens the meeting and frames the cross-functional question
beats.question: Call the C-suite meeting to order. Agenda: state of the bank this week. Do NOT consult any officer yet — that happens later, round the table. Right now just open the meeting and state, in one line each, the question you will put to the CFO, COO, CTO and CXO.
beats.answer:
**C-suite meeting is now in session.**

Agenda: state of the bank this week — financial health, operational posture, platform stability, and customer experience.

Round-the-table questions:

- **CFO:** What is our current financial position — profitability, net interest margin, RAROC, and capital adequacy — and how has it changed week-over-week?
- **COO:** What is the status of our money-movement rails, settlement cycles, float positions, and any operational incidents or near-misses this week?
- **CTO:** What is the current health of our platform — deployment cadence, system reliability, open incidents, and technical debt — and are there any emerging risks to availability or security?
- **CXO:** What does the customer experience look like this week — onboarding friction, NPS/CSAT trends, top customer complaints, and any CX incidents that demand executive attention?

beats.title: Round the table — CFO + COO
beats.shows: the CEO consults the finance + operations seats; figures attributed
beats.question: Go round the table. First the CFO: what do the books say this week (profitability / NIM / capital)? Then the COO: how are the payment rails and settlement running? Attribute every figure.
beats.answer:
**CFO and COO have reported. Here is the grounded synthesis, with every figure attributed.**

---

### FINANCE — CFO

The CFO reports that the ledger produces **monthly** snapshots only (July and August 2026), so the picture is month-over-month, not week-over-week.

**Profitability**
- Net income fell from **CAD 10,716.83 in July** to **CAD 3,292.88 in August**, a decrease of **CAD 7,423.95** (CFO).
- Return on Assets annualized dropped from **1.02% in July** to **0.27% in August** (CFO).
- Return on Equity annualized in August was **2.58%**; July had no ROE because the balance sheet showed only a CurrentEarnings equity account (CFO).
- The driver: interest income and interest expense both dropped to zero in August. The bank earned only **CAD 1,689.00 in fee income** and **CAD 1,603.88 in interchange income** (CFO).

**Net Interest Margin**
- NIM was **2.10% in July** and fell to exactly **0.00% in August** (CFO).
- Average earning assets actually grew from **CAD 4,080,233.65 in July** to **CAD 8,213,926.63 in August** (CFO).

**Risk-Adjusted Return on Capital**
- RAROC swung from **0.15% annualized in July** to **-9.13% annualized in August** (CFO).
- Expected credit loss for the period was **CAD 10,873.06 in August** versus **CAD 10,600.64 in July**, which exceeds the pre-provision net income of CAD 3,292.88 (CFO). *(Note: the CFO notes this expected loss is not reflected in net income or ROA/ROE because the ledger books no loan-loss provision.)*

**Capital Adequacy**
- Total assets grew from **CAD 12,395,833.63 in July** to **CAD 14,525,257.09 in August**, an increase of **CAD 2,129,423.46** (CFO).
- Total equity jumped from **CAD 10,716.83 in July** to **CAD 1,514,009.71 in August** (CAD 1,500,000.00 Capital account plus CAD 14,009.71 CurrentEarnings), an increase of **CAD 1,503,292.88** (CFO).
- Leverage ratio improved from **0.09% in July** to **10.42% in August** (CFO).
- RWA capital ratio improved from **0.12% in July** to **15.49% in August** (CFO).
- The CFO emphasizes this improvement is entirely due to a **CAD 1,500,000.00 equity injection** in August; without it, ratios would remain near zero.
- Loan-to-deposit ratio was **18.24× in July** and **7.66× in August** (CFO).

---

### OPERATIONS — COO

The COO reports for the week ending **2026-08-25**.

**Float Position**
- The COO's `float_position` tool returned a total system float of **-$12,162,225.08** (COO).
- Breakdown per the same tool: Lynx **-$10,441,107.71**; Cash **-$1,079,724.60**; AFT **-$394,355.12**; System **-$257,529.30**; Interac **+$10,491.65** (COO).
- The COO interprets the deeply negative Lynx and AFT accounts as normal clearing-account overdraft capacity, not a liquidity signal. The tool's basis note states these are "gross sum of system-account balances; components are signed per GL convention (clearing negative, external_cash exogenous) and are not economically additive — a magnitude, not a net position."

**Payment Rails & Settlement**
- **Interac:** **576 transactions** totaling **$89,146.14** — all deposited, clearing normally (COO).
- **AFT:** **0 transactions / $0** — dormant, no outbound settlement this week. There were 5 internal AFT holds and releases totaling **$6,172.80** (accumulator activity), but nothing reached the outbound batch (COO).
- **Lynx:** **0 transactions / $0** — dormant. Only activity was a single **$15,000.00 refund** from a prior stale-wire rejection (COO).
- **30-day context:** Lynx recall rate remains critically elevated — **4 recalls out of 16 wires (25.00% by count)** totaling **$4,399,756.24** in value. AFT shows **6 rejected entries ($243.00)** in the 30-day window (COO).

**Card Rail**
- **1,578 captured purchases** worth **$160,377.99** (COO).
- **75 active cardholders** (COO).
- **16 open authorization holds** totaling **$16,113.03** (COO).
- Approval rate: **89.91%**; decline rate: **10.09%**; NSF rate: **10.09%** (COO).
- Decline breakdown: **177 NSF declines / $55,472.97** (all via `card_authorize`); **57 limit declines / $24,317.01** (all via `withdrawal`) (COO).

**Operational Incidents**
- **Zero exceptions** this week: 0 failed transactions, 0 reversals, 0 returned AFT entries, 0 rejected AFT entries, 0 wire recalls (COO).
- The COO reviewed all four operational levers (`execute_cut_aft_batch`, `execute_sweep_expired_etransfers`, `execute_reject_stale_wires`, `execute_flush_notifications`) and found none warranted; no levers were pulled (COO).

---

**Cross-functional observation so far:** The bank's earnings engine has stalled — NIM is zero and net income collapsed in August. The COO shows that customer activity is concentrated almost entirely on cards and Interac, while wholesale rails (AFT, Lynx) are dormant. The 30-day Lynx recall rate of 25% remains a latent operational risk even though this week was clean. Capital ratios look healthy on paper only because of a recent equity injection.

Next up: the CTO and CXO.

contributions.text:
Here is the operational picture for the week ending 2026-08-25.

---

## 1. Float Position (point-in-time snapshot)

| System | Balance |
|--------|---------|
| **Total** | **-$12,162,225.08** |
| Lynx | -$10,441,107.71 |
| Cash | -$1,079,724.60 |
| AFT | -$394,355.12 |
| System | -$257,529.30 |
| Interac | +$10,491.65 |

**Interpretation:** The Lynx and AFT system accounts run deeply negative by design — these are clearing accounts with deliberate overdraft capacity so they can float on ordinary intraday timing without that being a liquidity signal. The negative sign means money has moved out through those rails; it is real economic activity, not missing cash. I treat this as a **revolving buffer**, not a static reserve, so I do not compare it against weekly volume totals.

---

## 2. Rail Status & Settlement Cycles (7-day window)

| Rail | Transactions | Value | Status |
|------|-------------|-------|--------|
| **Interac** | 576 | $89,146.14 | All **deposited** — clearing normally |
| **AFT** | 0 | $0 | **Dormant** — no outbound settlement this week |
| **Lynx** | 0 | $0 | **Dormant** — no wire settlement this week |

**Settlement cycles:**
- **Interac:** Running clean. 576 e-Transfer holds were placed and released, and all funds deposited.
- **AFT:** No rail settlement in the 7-day window. There were 5 internal AFT holds and 5 releases ($6,172.80), suggesting accumulator activity, but nothing reached the outbound batch for cutting.
- **Lynx:** No new wires settled. The only Lynx activity was a single **refund of $15,000.00** from a prior stale-wire rejection.

**30-day context:** Over the past 30 days, Lynx has had a critically elevated recall rate — 4 recalls out of 16 wires, which is **25.00%** by count and $4,399,756.24 by value. AFT shows 6 rejected entries ($243.00) in the 30-day window.

---

## 3. Card Rail (7-day window)

| Metric | Figure |
|--------|--------|
| Captured purchases | 1,578 |
| Captured value | $160,377.99 |
| Active cardholders | 75 |
| Open authorization holds (now) | 16 / $16,113.03 |
| Approval rate | 89.91% |
| Decline rate | 10.09% |
| NSF rate | 10.09% |

**Decline breakdown (7d):**
- **NSF:** 177 declines / $55,472.97 (all via `card_authorize`)
- **Limit:** 57 declines / $24,317.01 (all via `withdrawal`)

No validation, status, or "other" category declines this week. The card rail is the only channel showing consistent customer activity.

---

## 4. Operational Incidents & Near-Misses (7-day window)

**Exceptions:** **Zero** across the board.
- Failed transactions: 0
- Reversals: 0
- Returned AFT entries: 0
- Rejected AFT entries: 0
- Wire recalls: 0

**Verdict:** This was a **clean week** from an exceptions standpoint — no operational incidents or near-misses in the 7-day window.

**Caveat:** The persistent dormancy of AFT and Lynx outbound settlement remains a structural concern. The 30-day record shows prior AFT batch-accumulator blockages and Lynx recalls, but those did not recur as new exceptions this week.

---

## 5. Actions Taken

I reviewed all four operational levers against the current metrics:
- `execute_cut_aft_batch` — not warranted (no open outbound batch with entries)
- `execute_sweep_expired_etransfers` — not warranted (no expired e-Transfers)
- `execute_reject_stale_wires` — not warranted (no stale wires)
- `execute_flush_notifications` — not warranted (no backed-up notifications)

No levers were pulled. The bank's pre-checks would have refused them anyway.

---

**Summary:** Interac and card rails are carrying all of the operational load this week. Settlement on AFT and Lynx is frozen — not because of exceptions or blockages, but because there is simply no new outbound volume entering those rails. The float is stable and behaving as a revolving clearing buffer. The one item to watch is the 30-day Lynx recall rate, which remains elevated from prior weeks, but it produced no new exceptions this week.

**Important limitation first:** the ledger only produces **monthly** snapshots, not weekly. The two closed periods available are **July 2026** and **August 2026**. I therefore cannot speak to “this week” or “week-over-week” — the comparison below is **month-over-month** (July to August).

---

### 1. Profitability

- **Net income (31-day):**  
  - July 2026: CAD 10,716.83 (income_statement tool)  
  - August 2026: CAD 3,292.88 (income_statement tool)  
  - The compute tool shows a month-over-month decrease of CAD 7,423.95.

- **Return on Assets (annualized):**  
  - July: the key_ratios tool returned 0.010179390463887768, which converts to 1.02%.  
  - August: the key_ratios tool returned 0.002669213096290394, which converts to 0.27%.  
  - ROA therefore fell from 1.02% to 0.27%.

- **Return on Equity (annualized):**  
  - August: the key_ratios tool returned 0.025847337634408602, which converts to 2.58%.  
  - July had no ROE because the balance sheet showed only a CurrentEarnings equity account; the key_ratios tool returned null.

**What the books show:** August net income collapsed because interest income and interest expense both dropped to zero; the bank earned only fee income (CAD 1,689.00, income_statement tool) and interchange income (CAD 1,603.88, income_statement tool). ROA is now barely positive.

---

### 2. Net Interest Margin (NIM)

- **July 2026:** the nim tool returned 0.021029525458512612, which converts to 2.10% annualized. Average earning assets were CAD 4,080,233.65 (nim tool).
- **August 2026:** the nim tool returned 0E-26, i.e., 0.00%. Average earning assets were CAD 8,213,926.63 (nim tool).
- The compute tool shows the decimal difference as 0.02.

**What the books show:** NIM fell to exactly zero in August. The income statement shows zero interest income and zero interest expense, so there is no interest margin to speak of. Average earning assets actually grew, but the yield and cost of funds both went to zero.

---

### 3. Risk-Adjusted Return on Capital (RAROC)

- **July 2026:** the raroc tool returned 0.001472639018545353, which converts to 0.15% annualized.
- **August 2026:** the raroc tool returned -0.091314299788762028, which converts to -9.13% annualized.
- The compute tool shows the decimal difference as 0.09.

**What the books show:** RAROC swung from barely positive to deeply negative. The driver is that expected credit loss for the period was CAD 10,873.06 in August (the raroc tool returned 10873.064322739726 for expected_loss_period) versus CAD 10,600.64 in July (the raroc tool returned 10600.641435616438 for expected_loss_period), which far exceeds the pre-provision net income of CAD 3,292.88. The risk-adjusted return is therefore negative, meaning credit cost alone consumes all earnings and more. *(Note: the ledger books no loan-loss provision, so this expected loss is not reflected in net income or ROA/ROE — it is only visible in the RAROC tool.)*

---

### 4. Capital Adequacy

- **Total assets:**  
  - July: CAD 12,395,833.63 (balance_sheet tool)  
  - August: CAD 14,525,257.09 (balance_sheet tool)  
  - The compute tool shows an increase of CAD 2,129,423.46.

- **Total equity:**  
  - July: CAD 10,716.83 (balance_sheet tool, CurrentEarnings only)  
  - August: CAD 1,500,000.00 (balance_sheet tool, Capital account) plus CAD 14,009.71 (balance_sheet tool, CurrentEarnings). The compute tool sums this to CAD 1,514,009.71.  
  - The compute tool shows an increase of CAD 1,503,292.88.

- **Leverage ratio:**  
  - July: the key_ratios tool returned 0.0008645509709055364, which converts to 0.09%.  
  - August: the key_ratios tool returned 0.10423290277198116, which converts to 10.42%.  
  - The compute tool shows the decimal difference as 0.10.

- **RWA capital ratio:**  
  - July: the key_ratios tool returned 0.0011536341100473738, which converts to 0.12%.  
  - August: the key_ratios tool returned 0.1549018190276098, which converts to 15.49%.  
  - The compute tool shows the decimal difference as 0.15.

**What the books show:** Capital ratios improved dramatically, but this is entirely due to a **CAD 1,500,000.00 equity injection** that hit the Capital account in August (that account did not exist in July). Without that injection, the bank would still be running on retained earnings alone and the ratios would remain near zero. Even after the injection, the loan-to-deposit ratio was 7.66× in August (the key_ratios tool returned 7.657316384004445) and 18.24× in July (the key_ratios tool returned 18.241058459065743), indicating very high leverage in a business sense.

---

### Bottom line
- **Profitability:** Down sharply month-over-month; the bank stopped generating interest income in August.
- **NIM:** Zero — no interest margin at all.
- **RAROC:** Negative at approximately -9.13% annualized because expected credit cost (~CAD 10,873) dwarfs operating income.
- **Capital:** Ratios look much healthier on paper thanks to the CAD 1,500,000.00 equity injection, but the underlying earnings power is weak and credit risk remains high relative to income.

If you need a different period or want me to close a more recent month-end, let me know.

**Bottom line: yes, the platform is healthy.** Every signal I can see is green, there are no open incidents, and no operator action was needed or taken. Two persistent hygiene items remain on my watch list (details below).

## 1. System reliability — ✅ clean
- **Estate:** 19/19 deployments healthy across both clusters (nano-bank + modern-core), **0 degraded** — a 100.00% healthy share.
- **Crashloops:** none — the crashlooping list is **empty**.

## 2. Deployment cadence / delivery — ✅ clean
- **Rollouts:** 19 complete, 0 progressing, 0 stalled — 100.00% complete. Every deployment sits at a single active ReplicaSet (no half-rolled state).
- **Version drift:** none — the drift list is empty. Cross-cluster apps match: coredns `v1.10.1`, local-path-provisioner `v20230511-dc714da8`, postgres `16-alpine` on both clusters.

## 3. Open incidents — **none**
Nothing is degraded, stalled, or crashlooping, so neither recovery lever's precondition held and I took no action. Notably, the **recurring cfo stalled-rollout/CrashLoopBackOff pattern from prior reviews is absent** — cfo is desired 1 / ready 1 / available 1, rollout complete, pod `cfo-d469dcccf-mcmgp` at 0 restarts. That incident remains resolved.

## 4. Technical debt — two standing items (neither is a live fault)
1. **cfo's `/health` probes nothing.** It returns `ok=true` with an **empty checks map `{}`** — no dependency probes. Monitoring would have reported cfo "healthy" straight through its past stalled-rollout incidents. Recommend adding real dependency checks.
2. **Mutable image tags.** All `nano-*` app images run tag `dev`, and qdrant runs `latest`. With single-instance apps there's nothing to drift *against*, so the drift tool can't flag a bad or unexpected push — it would only surface at the next rollout. Recommend pinning immutable tags/digests.

- **Availability:** no active risk visible right now. - **Security:** I have no security, vulnerability, fraud, or AML telemetry in my tooling — I can't see that layer, so I won't assert anything about it. That's a gap to route to the appropriate security owner.
